description.value: Grape Savvy Wine Tours is an Indigenous-owned hop-on, hop-off trolley and private tour company operating in Penticton and along the Naramata Bench, founded by Métis entrepreneur Savannah 'Savvy' Swaisland. The company offers curated winery tours, corporate charters, wedding transportation, and the unique 'Saddle Up & Sip' experience developed in collaboration with Syilx/Okanagan-owned businesses. For touring cyclists, it represents a way to extend a wine-country visit without pedalling between stops, and the hop-on, hop-off format means bikes could potentially be left at a hub while riders explore by trolley.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is fully available and describes an active, Indigenous-owned wine tour and trolley transportation company based in Penticton, BC. Phone (250-460-1242) and email (info@grapesavvy.ca) are confirmed on multiple website pages. No bike-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the site; the business is a tour operator, not a food/drink establishment, though it is listed under Food & Drink in the OSM record.
concerns: Category is listed as 'Food & Drink' in OSM but this is a tour operator and transportation company, not a food or drink retailer. Consider recategorizing to Tours & Activities or Transportation.
No physical street address is available in OSM or on the website — the business appears to operate from vehicles/trolleys rather than a fixed storefront, which may affect map pin accuracy.
OSM record has no osm_id and empty osm_tags, suggesting this was added manually rather than from a verified OSM node.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly bookable business with a live website, confirmed contact details, and seasonal trolley operations in the Penticton/Naramata wine country — directly relevant to touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan.
enrichment_extras.notes: The 'Saddle Up & Sip' tour is explicitly developed in collaboration with Syilx/Okanagan-owned businesses and represents an Indigenous cultural tourism experience. The trolleys are not wheelchair accessible per the FAQ. Trolley service runs weekends only.
